evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: “Content identification” and “fingerprinting” can mean different techniques/sources (audio fingerprinting vs metadata/ID matching), leading to materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: “My profile” is underspecified (listening history, demographics, preferences, explicit settings), allowing different interpretations of what data drives discovery.

evaluations.evidence: based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is undefined (taste similarity, demographics, behavior), which changes the requirement materially.

evaluations.evidence: music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Content similarity” is ambiguous (audio similarity, visual similarity, metadata similarity, or a combination), leading to different system behavior.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags ... related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path
evaluations.rationale: “Enriched metadata,” “image tags,” and “relevant listening path” are vague abstractions that permit multiple materially different interpretations of inputs and outputs.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: “Tags” and “all further processing steps” are unclear (which tag schema? which pipeline steps?), enabling different interpretations of scope and persistence.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: “Thumbnail sequences” and “video segments” are underspecified (how segments are defined; what constitutes a sequence), leading to different UI/segmentation requirements.

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Info” and “similar” are undefined, and “items and segments” could refer to different entity types; this allows materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Perceptually similar” is ambiguous (visual-only, audio-only, multimodal; which perceptual features), changing the requirement materially.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: Both “content” (what types) and “similar profiles” (similarity definition) are unclear, enabling different recommendation behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: “Most relevant” and “my area” are vague (relevance criteria; geographic granularity), leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” could mean detect faces vs recognize specific individuals; “related information” is also unspecified, yielding materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” (detect category vs specific product/SKU) and “related information” are unclear, allowing different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Related information” is underspecified (channel name, program, links, metadata), leading to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify brands” could mean detect brand logos vs infer brand from context; “related information” is vague.

evaluations.evidence: recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: “Related” is ambiguous (visual similarity, same topic, same location, same objects), producing materially different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: walk around, access content using a geographical map ... videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: “Covering the area” and “relevant point of interest” are vague (coverage definition; relevance criteria), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: “Using automatic speech recognition” is underspecified (search by transcript keywords, speaker, language; real-time vs batch), allowing different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” is ambiguous (shot boundaries, scenes, semantic segments) and “validate” criteria are unspecified, leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: “Topic” is undefined (taxonomy vs free-text; single vs multiple topics), which materially affects the requirement.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: “A/V quality aspects” is vague (resolution, bitrate, loudness, noise, artifacts, etc.), enabling different ranking/filtering criteria.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: “Edited” is ambiguous (cut/splice, compression, noise reduction, normalization) and “quick assessment” is vague, leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: “Nudity content” is ambiguous (partial vs full nudity; artistic/medical exceptions), which changes filtering behavior materially.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: “Low-level asset information” is an unclear abstraction (file properties vs signal features), allowing multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: “Validated” and “copyright infringement” detection scope are ambiguous (match thresholds, what constitutes infringement), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user
evaluations.rationale: “High-level asset information” and “recognized by the system” are vague; also unclear which metadata/tags and how they are used for prefiltering.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting,” “appealing,” and “complex” are subjective and undefined, enabling materially different interpretations of the assessment.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should be prompted” lacks criteria/thresholds; “look at a subject” is also vague, leading to different triggering rules.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: “Volunteer types” is undefined (skill level, engagement segments, roles), allowing multiple materially different categorizations.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassify” (into what classes) and “simple low-level image features” are underspecified, enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: detect Snapshot Serengeti images with no classifiable animals in them
evaluations.rationale: The intent is clear: flag images lacking animals that can be classified; while thresholds could vary, the requirement does not present multiple materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: “Image series detection” and what constitutes “timestamping malfunction” are unclear, leading to different detection/repair behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” is ambiguous without specifying target species set/taxonomy and output form (labels vs probabilities).

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Attribute” is undefined (age, sex, behavior, markings, etc.), allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal number detection
evaluations.rationale: “Number detection” is ambiguous (count individuals visible, estimate total present, handle occlusion), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation or localization” are different tasks and the story does not specify which is required (or both), creating ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: detect Plankton Portal images with no classifiable plankton in them
evaluations.rationale: The requirement is straightforward: identify images lacking plankton that can be classified; no materially different interpretations are implied by the wording.

evaluations.evidence: detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: “Size” (area, length, bounding box, scale calibration) and “orientation” (angle definition) are underspecified, enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: “Species” set/taxonomy and what “preclassification” outputs are not specified, allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: “Reduce video duration” is ambiguous (speed-up, trim inactive segments, summarize), leading to materially different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time ... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: The requirement is specific: identify the timestamp/event of egg-laying in a video; it does not invite multiple materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc
evaluations.rationale: “Important features” is vague and the “etc” leaves scope open-ended, allowing materially different feature sets and detection goals.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: “Probability/weight” is ambiguous (confidence score, trust weight, calibration) and “experience” is undefined, leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: “Remove artefacts” is ambiguous (mask, delete, correct, filter out images) and examples do not fully define scope, enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects
evaluations.rationale: “Transient” is undefined (timescale/criteria) and detection output expectations are unclear, allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds
evaluations.rationale: “Background noise” and especially “distracting sounds” are subjective/undefined, leading to materially different filtering requirements.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is undefined (frequency patterns, call type, duration, species), enabling different grouping criteria.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard in a single audio file
evaluations.rationale: “Number of whales heard” is ambiguous (distinct individuals vs simultaneous callers; handling repeats/overlap), leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Should interrupt” lacks criteria and “interrupt” could mean different interventions (popup, message, task stop), creating ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Still ambiguous because “interrupt” conditions are unspecified and the choice logic among modalities is not defined.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Should educate” is undefined (triggers, thresholds, goals), allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous because the decision criteria for modality selection and what counts as “educate” are not specified.

evaluations.evidence: which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Piece of education” is undefined (lesson, hint, tutorial, FAQ item) and selection criteria are unclear, enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: interesting comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting” is subjective/undefined and “subject” could mean different entities (image, discussion thread, classification item), creating ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should comment” lacks triggering criteria and “subject” is unclear, allowing multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: “Should give an explanation” is underspecified (what triggers; what constitutes an explanation), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Should say” is open-ended without constraints (tone, content types, templates, contexts), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Subjects” and “similarity” are undefined (which subject type; similarity features/metric), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects to volunteers based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: “Previous experiences” is ambiguous (projects joined, tasks completed, performance, interests), leading to different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: “Summary” (length/type) and “articles” (which sources/types) are underspecified; “reuse them” is also unclear, enabling different interpretations.
